Synopsis:
    U.S. senior officials allege COSCO, China's state-owned shipping giant, operates concealed signals intelligence equipment aboard its vessels to collect military communications data near coastlines of target nations including the U.S. and Europe. The arrangement is described as a decades-long intelligence partnership with Beijing. COSCO is already on the Pentagon's military-linked companies list. Geopolitical context includes an expiring U.S.-China trade détente (November deadline), a planned Trump-Xi summit in September, and a previously paused plan to impose heavy port fees on Chinese shippers. Removing COSCO from U.S. supply chains is flagged as economically disruptive.
